objective.statement: Halve the measured latency of GET /items in src/items.js, measured with bench/bench.mjs before and after.
objective.success_definition: The measured latency of GET /items, as measured by bench/bench.mjs, is at most half of the baseline measurement taken before the change, with the test suite still green.

goals.statement: Reduce the measured latency of GET /items in src/items.js to at most half of its pre-change measured value.
acceptance: bench/bench.mjs run before the change records a baseline latency for GET /items
bench/bench.mjs run after the change shows GET /items latency at or below 50% of the recorded baseline

goals.statement: Keep the existing test suite passing.
acceptance: The project's test suite passes after the change

constraints.statement: Do not change the public response envelope.
Latency must be measured with bench/bench.mjs before and after the change.

assumptions.statement: bench/bench.mjs is an existing, runnable benchmark script that reports latency for GET /items.
A test suite exists and can be run to confirm it stays green.

open_questions.question: What command runs the test suite, and what command runs bench/bench.mjs (e.g., node bench/bench.mjs)?
Is the latency target a strict 50% reduction of the measured baseline, and which reported metric (mean, p50, p95) counts as 'the measured latency'?
options: Mean latency at or below 50% of baseline
p50 latency at or below 50% of baseline
p95 latency at or below 50% of baseline

verification.spec: Run bench/bench.mjs before the change and record the baseline latency of GET /items; run it again after the change and compare.
verification.expected: Post-change measured latency of GET /items is at most 50% of the recorded baseline.

verification.spec: Run the project's test suite after the change.

deliverables.description: Modification to src/items.js that reduces GET /items latency to at most half of the measured baseline without caching, new dependencies, new endpoints, or changes to the public response envelope.

factors: A 50% latency reduction may not be achievable without caching depending on the current implementation.
Benchmark variance could make the before/after comparison unreliable.
Optimizations risk subtly altering response behavior despite the envelope constraint.
